content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble accessing a customized webserver that's programmed with [product_name] using [version_no]. When I export the project ([product_name]) to the uSD card through ethernet, I can view the webserver main page and standard webserver interface, but the customized page returns a 404 error (target not found). The only workaround I've found is exporting the project directly to the uSD card connected to the PC. I tried different browsers and private modes, but after downloading via ethernet, the 404 persists. Can anyone tell me what I'm doing wrong?
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Is it possible that the folder in which your [product_name] project is saved on your PC shares the same name as the project itself?

Hi [user_name], thanks for the welcome. I've resolved the issue. Although the project and [product_name] folder had different names, the [product_name] files were inside two subfolders both named 'x'. By moving the files directly under the 'webserver' folder, the problem disappeared. Thanks for your suggestion, it helped solve my issue.
Hello [user_name], glad to hear it's working now!
Could you please explain the steps to solve this? I appreciate a step-by-step guide, thank you.
Please clarify your specific problem so we can assist you more effectively.

analysis.insight_summary: A user experienced a 404 error when trying to access a customized web server created with [product_name] and deployed via ethernet to a uSD card. Main and standard webserver pages loaded, but custom pages didn't, revealing the importance of the correct file/folder structure when exporting these projects. This highlights how mismanaged folder hierarchy can lead to deployment issues and user confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a simple, reliable process for deploying custom webserver pages, regardless of folder structure, and desire clearer guidance to avoid common file management errors.
